title: Class Strategy
definition: Implementing dark mode manually by toggling a CSS class via JavaScript, allowing the user to override their OS preferences.
simpleExplanation: A user's iPhone is in Light Mode, but they are reading your blog at 2 AM and their eyes hurt. They click your 'Dark Mode' button. Your React state updates, slapping `<html class="dark">` onto the page. Suddenly, all `dark:bg-black` classes instantly activate, saving their eyes.
realWorldExample: Creating a Theme Context in React that manages a `theme` state (`light` or `dark`), saves that preference to `localStorage`, and injects it into the DOM on page load.

basic: In the class strategy, what exact class name must be present on a parent element to trigger dark mode?
intermediate: Why do you need to save the user's theme choice to `localStorage`?

answers.question: Why localStorage?
answers.answer: If you don't save it to `localStorage`, the website will reset back to Light Mode every single time the user clicks a link to a new page or refreshes the browser.
